newsitem.title: USA: Santee Cooper, MEAG, JEA utilities join to market.
newsitem.headline: Santee Cooper, MEAG, JEA utilities join to market.

text.p: Three of the South's biggest municipal electric authorities announced Monday they would form a new agency to jointly market wholesale power.

Joining to form The Energy Authority are the South Carolina Public Service Authority, also known as Santee Cooper; the Municipal Electric Authority of Georgia; and the Jacksonville (Florida) Electric Authority.
The new agency will begin operations in August and will be located in Jacksonville, spokesman Nick Bane said.
The utilities said the agreement would enable them to ensure competitive pricing and reliability of energy supplies. Currently, each markets power separately.

The new power-marketing alliance will assume buying and selling responsibilities for the agencies via a seven-day, 24-hour operation that participates in the short- mid- and long-term markets, the utilities said.

In a joint statement, the three utilities said, "Our proposed power-marketing alliance is simply an extension of joint-action initiatives that have long been a means to increase the value of public power for its stakeholders.

"Through improved efficiencies, productivity and enhanced capabilities in the wholesale market, we can better leverage our generation assets and ensure the competitiveness of wholesale power sales and purchases," they said.
The Energy Authority will be governed by a nine-member board of directors, with three from each utility.

Santee Cooper is the nation's fourth largest publicly owned electric utility, owning and controlling over 3,600 megawatts of generation. It serves 109,000 retail customers and generates power for 377,000 customers served by 15 of South Carolina's 20 electric cooperatives.

JEA is Florida's largest and the nation's eighth largest municipally owned electric utility. It owns and controls 3,000 megawatts of generating capacity and serves 330,000 customers in northeast Florida.

MEAG Power is the nation's largest joint-action agency, an alliance of several electric utilities or municipalities formed to acquire generation and transmission resources or services. MEAG generates power for 49 municipal utilities in Georgia, serving 635,000 customers, and owns 1,558 megawatts of generation.
The utiliites are linked through transmission interconnections in South Carolina, Georgia and Florida.
